pg007_n0008: In this chapter, you will learn about the concept of drama and acting, and types of acting.

pg007_n0021: Drama and acting are very important concepts in the performing arts as they play a major role in conveying messages to the intended audience.
pg007_n0022: Therefore, developing an insight into these concepts is essential in building skills in the field of acting.
pg007_n0024: Drama is a type of performing art that aims to convey a message to a live audience.
pg007_n0025: In a drama performance, both the audience and the actor are present in the same place at the same time.
pg007_n0026: In other forms of performing arts, such as music and film, this simultaneous presence of the two groups does not occur, or it is not necessary.
pg007_n0028: There are two types of drama performed on stage.
pg007_n0029: The first type is written scripts, and the second type is improvised drama.
pg007_n0030: The scripted drama differs from improvised drama because it requires long time to study and memorise the lines; while improvised drama depends on creativity of the actors.
pg008_n0002: Acting is a way of conveying a message to the audience through actions and word.
pg008_n0003: Also, it is recognised as a career that requires the performer to be creative in conveying the message to the intended audience.
pg008_n0004: The main performers are human beings who use their bodies and voices in a play to convey the message to the audience in a way that is engaging and easy to understand.
pg008_n0005: Performers are required to be creative in various areas, including:
pg008_n0009: Using the body and voice creatively and skilfully;
pg008_n0012: Learn the audience and create the message according to their culture, interests and needs;

pg009_n0010: Aspects to consider when acting with actions and voice
pg009_n0012: Acting that involves both actions and voice requires careful attention and thorough preparation.
pg009_n0013: The following are some important aspects to consider in this type of acting:
pg009_n0018: Understanding the character you are portraying.
pg009_n0019: It is essential to understand the character’s personality, background and goals.
pg009_n0020: Additionally, develop an awareness of the character’s emotions in each scene and how they can be expressed through actions and voice.
pg009_n0021: It is important to know how the character walks, speaks and struggles to achieve their objectives.
pg009_n0025: Mastering the use of body language.
pg009_n0026: Ensure that your body movements match the emotions you are intending to portray.
pg009_n0029: Use your hands and facial expressions to convey different emotions such as happiness, sadness, surprise, or anger, rather than relying on words only.
pg010_n0006: To perform effectively on stage, control your voice by adjusting tone, speed and volume according to the context in reflecting the character’s emotions.
pg010_n0007: Ensure that your voice and pronunciation are clear and audible to the audience.
pg010_n0012: Make sure you portray the character you are acting realistically.
pg010_n0013: Avoid repetitive habits or uses of the same emotions in each scene.
pg010_n0018: Make sure that you listen and respond appropriately to the conversation initiated by your fellow performers during rehearsals.
pg010_n0019: Make an attempt of maintaining good communication with them as you perform on stage in front of the audience.
pg010_n0024: To perform well on stage, make sure you are confident and seen by your audience.
pg010_n0026: Do not stay in one area for the entire time of your performance on stage.
pg010_n0027: Engage the audience through your creative use of body and voice while acting.
pg010_n0031: Practise regularly to improve your voice and appearance on stage.
pg010_n0032: Develop a habit of improving your acting skills.
pg010_n0033: Read scripts of plays or watch films that showcase stage performances and imitate the characters using your gestures and voice.
pg010_n0038: The actor should make sure that the voice and actions match.
pg010_n0039: For example, a performer portraying sadness should not use a strong voice or presents signs of excitement while on stage.

pg013_n0004: It is a form of performing arts in which performers use actions without words to convey a message to the audience.
pg013_n0005: It is a powerful type of acting that relies entirely on body language, such as gestures, posture, and facial expressions, to convey messages without using words.
pg013_n0006: The origin of mime can be traced back to early human history when the first human beings began to struggle with their lives.
pg013_n0007: They used body language to communicate at a time when spoken language had not yet been discovered.
pg013_n0008: For this reason, body language is considered an ancient form of communication that human beings used in the earliest stages of interaction.
pg013_n0010: As a form of performing arts, mime became popular in the 20th century.
pg013_n0011: It was widely used in theatre and became a key element in early films, before the invention of sound technology.
pg013_n0012: These early silent films relied completely on the actors’ ability to express themselves through mime to tell stories and engage viewers emotionally.
pg013_n0013: Despite the advancements of technology and the development of sound in media, mime continues to hold an important place in both film and theatre.
pg013_n0014: It is still used today in stage performances, movies and other forms of artistic expression.
pg013_n0015: Mime also goes beyond the stage.
pg013_n0016: People use gestures and body language in everyday situations to communicate when words are not available or necessary.

pg014_n0009: Mime depends on the body to convey messages.
pg014_n0010: This means performers must develop skills to use their body parts to communicate with the audience without relying on words.
pg014_n0011: This type of acting incorporates key elements such as body movements, music, emotions, facial expressions, symbols, sound effects and pantomime to convey a message.
pg014_n0012: Examples of pantomimic movements include closing an imaginary door or holding an imaginary cup.
pg014_n0013: All pantomime performances are accompanied by music or narration.

pg014_n0018: Important things to consider in mime
pg014_n0020: There are several important aspects to consider in mime, including:
pg014_n0026: The body is the primary tool in mime.
pg014_n0027: It is used to express thoughts and emotions using the body to reflect the intended message to the audience through the character you are portraying.
pg014_n0032: Use your body to express the emotions of your character, such as confidence, sadness, anxiety, or joy.
pg014_n0033: For example, you might jump or laugh to presents great happiness.
pg014_n0038: The face is an important part of showing various emotions because it has many muscles that can be used to express different emotions such as happiness, sadness, anger, fear or surprise.
pg014_n0039: Ensure that the facial expressions you display are clear and easily visible to the audience.
pg014_n0044: Make sure actions involving invisible objects are realistic by considering their size, weight, and direction.
pg014_n0045: This includes using body movements, posture, and gestures when interacting with imaginary objects, such as opening a door, carrying a heavy load, or holding a light ball.
pg015_n0006: Ensure that the pace of your acting movements matches the scene’s context.
pg015_n0007: For example, if you act as if you are climbing a steep mountain, do not walk at a normal pace as if you are on flat ground.
pg015_n0012: Maintain eye contact with the audience to keep them involved in the performance.
pg015_n0013: Body postures and positioning in facing the audience are the main tools that will help you ensure your audience is watching and following the performance.
pg015_n0014: Develop the skill to communicate with your audience using your eyes.
pg015_n0018: Organisation and flow of the performance.
pg015_n0019: Ensure the performance has a smooth and logical flow from beginning to end.
pg015_n0020: The sequence should be easy to follow, even without sound or words.
pg015_n0025: Mime requires physical strength and flexibility.
pg015_n0026: Regular stage exercises can help improve body movements and performance.
pg015_n0030: Use of music and sound effects.
pg015_n0031: In mime, music and sound effects can be used to enhance emotions and guide the story.
pg015_n0032: They help the audience understand the scene more effectively.
pg015_n0036: This art form plays a significant role in society and the world of performing arts.
pg015_n0041: Promoting the traditions and customs of the nation both locally and internationally;
pg015_n0044: Helping actors and others understand how to use their bodies to convey messages effectively;
pg015_n0047: Fostering creativity as it requires significant creativity to express emotions and events through body movements and gestures;
pg015_n0050: Serving as a teaching tool, especially for children and people with hearing impairments;
pg015_n0053: Entertaining as it is a unique and captivating form of performing art;
pg015_n0056: Touching deeply the emotions of the audience because it compels people to understand the message by observing gestures and movements only; and
pg015_n0060: Developing acting talent in mime,whereas actors learn to channel their emotions without relying on words.
pg015_n0061: This makes them better performers in other forms of acting.

pg016_n0011: Although it is a very important form of acting, mime faces several challenges, including:
pg016_n0015: It is difficult for actors to convey a message to the audience if they do not have sufficient skill;
pg016_n0018: Mime requires a long time of practise and rehearsal to convey a message to the audience;
pg016_n0021: Limited understanding of the audience, as not everyone has the ability to interpret performances that do not use words to convey the message, making some messages not easily understood;
pg016_n0023: Despite these challenges, mime as a form of acting remains an important art form that requires patience, creativity and dedication to make it more engaging and effective.

pg018_n0014: How musical dynamics and vocal balance improve singing
pg018_n0018: Musical dynamics involve changes in the level of the volume during singing or playing a musical instrument.
pg018_n0019: These changes involve increasing or decreasing the volume.
pg018_n0020: It is important for a singer or an instrumentalist to know when to increase the volume and when to decrease it.
pg018_n0021: This helps to convey a message and make the emotion of the song clearer.
pg018_n0022: Often, lowering the volume is one of the ways of achieving a soft or gentle sound.
pg018_n0023: Music dynamics help a listener to understand and feel the emotions expressed through the song.

pg020_n0015: It is crucial in singing by involving multiple voices at the same time to achieve a harmonious blend.

pg021_n0017: This method makes it easier to learn accurate note singing and helps improve the ability to read and write music.

pg021_n0024: Musical notes are symbols used to represent duration in written music.
pg021_n0025: Musical notes indicate the duration for which a particular note should be sung or played accurately.
pg021_n0026: In music, there are different types of notes such as whole notes, half notes and quarter notes.
pg021_n0027: Normally, a whole note lasts four beats, a half note lasts two beats, and a quarter note lasts one beat.
pg021_n0028: These musical notes differ in length, so in singing a major scale using solfa, we choose the type of note,

pg026_n0004: Musical instruments play a major role in helping to understand the voice, note arrangement, and musical relationships in practice.

pg029_n0004: Using shapes in drawing is a basic method that helps create accurate and well-structured drawings.

pg029_n0022: Observe the size of the shape and space within to presents the proportion of the object you are drawing;
pg029_n0025: Use sketch lines to get a map of the real image before drawing it, then draw the real image following those lines; and
pg029_n0028: Add shadows to the shapes in order to acquire depth and realism of the image.
pg029_n0032: Drawing using a circular shape is very important in artwork.

pg049_n0020: Flowerpots are containers used to keep flowers.
pg049_n0021: These pots can be made using clay or cement.
pg049_n0022: Cement pots are placed in a special place for a while to dry, then carved and finally filled with flowers.
pg049_n0023: Clay pots must be dried and finally fired to make them stronger.
pg049_n0024: Pots can be made by using pinching, coiling, slab, wheel throwing, and moulding techniques.
pg049_n0028: This is a method used to model pots by using a moulding technique.
pg049_n0029: You must first prepare a mould of the shape you prefer to make.
pg049_n0030: A mould is a tool that is made first to give shape to other vessels by the casting method.
pg049_n0031: The caster presses the soft clay into the mould and stays there for a while until it dries, and then it is removed, having already copied the shape of the mould.
pg049_n0032: By using a mould, you get the advantage of moulding many similar objects in a short time.

pg050_n0004: Materials used to make a mould
pg050_n0006: Materials used in making a mould include clay, water, cement, sand, a mould sample, a levelling trowel, a thick rope about the size of a thumb, a flowerpot, wire mesh, scissors, newspapers and liquid glue.
pg050_n0007: Other materials include thin wood, dry leaves, matches, cotton cloth, a small brush, a small knife, oil paints, kerosene, paint containers, a spade, a trowel and a plastic bucket or thick nylon and light nylon bags.
pg050_n0011: Moulding for pots begins with creating two halves of a mould, which, when joined, form a complete pot shaped like the one you intend to make.
pg050_n0012: To create a mould for a pot, follow these steps:
pg050_n0016: Select a flowerpot that has a form and size of your choice, then clean it thoroughly to remove any dirt or residues;
pg050_n0019: Cover the flowerpot with a piece of newspaper using a strong adhesive or glue.
pg050_n0020: Make sure the newspaper is smooth and has no wrinkles to create an even surface;
pg050_n0023: Stick a rope vertically along the flowerpot.
pg050_n0024: This will divide the pot into two halves, allowing you to create a two-part mould as shown in Figure 2.
pg050_n0025: Make sure to let the glue dry completely before proceeding with the next steps in your mould-making process.
pg051_im001: A pot covered with newspaper pieces. A rope runs down the middle to divide it into two halves.
pg051_n0002: Figure 2: A pot glued with newspapers and divided into halves by a rope
pg051_n0006: Prepare a plaster mixture by mixing sand, cement, and a small amount of water;
pg051_n0009: Measure and cut the wire mesh to fit both sides of the flowerpot;
pg051_n0012: Apply a 2cm thick layer of plaster to the flowerpot, and use a piece of rope to divide the plaster into two halves.
pg051_n0013: Once the first layer is set, place the wire mesh onto the soft plaster on both sides of the pot.
pg051_n0014: Then, add a second layer of plaster to fully cover the wire mesh on both sides, ensuring the rope remains exposed;
pg051_n0017: Smooth the edges of both sides of the pot properly;
pg051_n0020: Put the pot in the shade to allow it to dry, as seen in Figure 3.

pg057_n0012: Flowerpots made of clay must be fired to make them strong.
pg057_n0013: The fired flowerpots are resistant to erosion, even when saturated with water.
pg057_n0014: The firing of these pots occurs in an open kiln, which differs from an interior kiln.
pg057_n0015: An interior kiln is a small building equipped with a door for passing pots and air, as well as a designated firing area and a smoke tunnel.
pg057_n0016: In contrast, an open kiln is simply a designated outdoor space where thin pieces of firewood and dry leaves are arranged in a slight pit to start the firing process.
pg057_n0017: The key to effective firing is maintaining constant heating, which is why firewood and dry leaves are preferred materials.
pg057_n0019: Steps to be followed in clay pot firing in the open kiln

pg057_n0031: Carefully arrange the clay pots that you want to fire on top of the layer of dry grass and firewood;
pg057_n0034: Add another layer of dry leaves and additional firewood to cover the pots completely.
pg057_n0035: Once ready, light the fire to begin the firing process.

pg072_n0009: Steps for making baskets using paper materials
pg072_n0014: Cut the paper into long strips about 1 to 2 centimetres wide.
pg072_n0015: Use a pencil or a thin stick to roll each strip tightly to form a tube-like shape;
pg072_n0018: Create the base of the basket.
pg072_n0019: Take eight to ten paper tubes and arrange them in a star shape (intersecting at the centre).
pg072_n0020: Use glue to stick them together at the centre, and wait for them to dry;
pg072_n0024: Take one paper tube and begin wrapping it around the base tubes.
pg072_n0025: Weave by alternating the tube over and under the base tubes in sequence.
pg072_n0026: Continue weaving in a circular motion, ensuring each layer is firm and close together;
pg072_n0029: Increase the size of the basket.
pg072_n0030: When you reach the end of a paper tube, glue on another one and continue weaving.
pg072_n0031: Repeat this process until the basket wall reaches the desired height;
pg072_n0034: Finalise the top of the basket.
pg072_n0035: Trim the base tubes with scissors to match the basket’s height.
pg072_n0036: Fold the ends inward and glue them down to create a neat rim; and
pg072_n0040: Enhance the appearance of the basket by adding decorative cords or extra embellishments.

pg099_n0004: To be able to play netball well, a player must have the basic skills of the game.

pg099_n0009: Passing is the act of throwing the ball from one player to another of the same team.
pg099_n0010: Passing accurately is essential for a team to attack quickly and prevent opponents from gaining possession of the ball.
pg099_n0011: The main types of passes are chest pass, bounce pass and high pass.
pg099_n0015: A chest pass is the throwing of the ball, released from the passer’s chest, directly to the teammate’s chest using both hands.
pg099_n0016: The pass is normally quick, easy and accurate to short distances.
pg099_n0017: To be successful, the player must hold the ball with both hands and place it in front of the chest, then push it powerfully and accurately towards the teammate, as shown in Figure 10.

pg100_n0004: A bounce pass is the passing of the ball whereby the ball is thrown so as to bounce once before it reaches the receiving player.
pg100_n0005: The ball is held with two hands while directing it to the bouncing point and released at an angle to bounce hard towards the teammate.
pg100_n0006: This type of pass prevents the opponent from catching it as the ball is strategically directed to a teammate.
pg100_n0007: It is often done for a short distance, as shown in Figure 11.

pg100_n0014: This pass is often used when a player needs to deliver the ball over a long distance or when they want the ball to go over the obstacles of the opposing team.
pg100_n0015: To make this pass, the player stands upright, takes the ball with both hands behind the head, and then pushes it forward with force and accuracy to reach the distant player, as shown in Figure 12.

Mime is a type of performing art.
Performers use actions without words to give a message to the audience.
pg013_n0005_easy_read:
Mime is a strong type of acting.

Body language includes:
- gestures
- posture
- facial expressions
pg013_n0006_easy_read:
Mime started in early human history.
It began when the first human beings struggled to live.
pg013_n0007_easy_read:

People had not discovered spoken language yet.
pg013_n0008_easy_read:

pg013_n0010_easy_read: Mime became popular as a performing art in the 20th century.

People used mime a lot in theatre.
It also became an important part of early films, before sound technology was invented.

pg013_n0013_easy_read:
Technology advanced, and sound developed in media.
But mime still has an important place in film and theatre.

People still use mime today in:
- stage performances
- movies
- other forms of artistic expression
pg013_n0015_easy_read: Mime is also used outside the stage.
